verdict.reasoning: Patient reports painful urination for a few days: "it's uh, hurting when I... pee. And um, it's been going on for a few days" and doctor summarizes "last three days, you've been having bit of burning pain on passing urine."
Patient notes lower abdominal pain with voiding: "I also maybe sometimes get some like, pain kind of lower down in my tummy, when I, when I go to the bathroom" and describes it as "sort of cramping."
Patient reports abnormal urine smell: "It does kind of, it, it kind of like, doesn't smell very, it smells a bit weird I guess."
Patient describes a small episode of hematuria today: "there was a little bit of blood earlier today, um, but besides that, not at all, no."
Past medical history includes IBS: "in the past I've had some uh, some IBS."
She denies regular medications: Doctor: "Do you take any regular medications?" Patient: "Uh, no" which supports that she is taking no ongoing medications.

She reports recent bicarbonate use without benefit: "I did uh, a little bit ago, or a couple of days ago, try some uh, over the counter bicarbonate, to try and help with the pain but it wasn't, it wasn't really helping."

Allergy to clindamycin with swelling is documented: Patient: "yeah, I'm allergic to, Clindamycin." Doctor: "And what happens when you take Clindamycin?" Patient: "I get some like a, a, a swelling, basically."
She denies relevant family history: Doctor asks about "related to kidneys, bladder, bowels, guts?" Patient: "no I don't think so, not that I, not anything I know about."
She is a biology student living with friends: "I live in a flat near my college, with a couple of like friends of mine" and later "I'm a student" / "I'm studying biology."
She denies smoking: Doctor: "do you, do you smoke" Patient: "I don't, I don't smoke."
She drinks alcohol socially on weekends: Patient: "I do drink, like on the weekends" and doctor clarifies "so socially, OK."

Doctor’s assessment is a simple UTI with described symptoms: "I think probably do have what we call a simple UTI or urinary tract infection" and summarizes "last three days, you've been having bit of burning pain on passing urine. A bit of, crampy tummy pain lower down"; urine malodor was reported earlier by patient.

Doctor plans Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim for 3 days, BID: "I'll give you a course of antibiotics today. Something, called either Nitrofurantoin, or Trimethoprim. Uh, and it's normally a three day course. Uh, so, one tablet, twice a day, for three days."
Hydration and cranberry juice are advised: "I also advise you to drink plenty of fluids" and "You can try, cranberry juice, that can sometimes help with your symptoms."

Doctor advises avoiding intercourse until symptoms clear and continuing condoms: "if you can try and avoid it, I think that'd be sensible" and "It's great that you're using barrier contraception. I would recommend you to continue using barrier contraception, but if you can avoid it while your symptoms clear up."

Follow-up and red-flag instructions given: "if you're still not better, by the end of this week, I want you to give me a call or come back and see me" and later "things to look out for would be... high temperatures, a back pain, ... generally feeling more unwell... do give me a call if you're having any concerns."
